name: M.K.Sons Fine Jewels
summary: M.K.Sons Fine Jewels retails gold, diamond and CZ jewellery through five showrooms in Mumbai and Ahmedabad, sourcing all its products from third-party manufacturers and karigars; the Ahmedabad showrooms brought in about 68% of FY26 revenue. Revenue grew from ₹217 cr in FY24 to ₹539 cr in FY26 and profit rose 123% in FY26 to ₹51.8 cr, with the net margin widening to 9.6%. Operating cash flow was negative in FY24, FY25 and the June 2026 quarter and only ₹15.4 cr in FY26, as inventory days rose to 193. About 69% of the ₹220 cr fresh issue funds inventory for a new and an expanded showroom, and at the upper band the post-issue P/E of about 17.6x is below the median of the listed peers named in the RHP.

fh1.finding: Revenue from operations rose from ₹217.3 cr (FY24) to ₹538.7 cr (FY26), a CAGR of about 57.4%.

fh2.finding: Revenue grew every year: ₹217 cr, ₹351 cr, ₹539 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh3.finding: Debt to equity was 0.39 at June 2026 (borrowings ₹70.5 cr vs net worth ₹183.0 cr).

fh4.finding: Borrowings rose 77% (₹38.6 cr to ₹68.4 cr) while total income rose 148% over FY24–FY26.

fh5.finding: Net worth rose every year: ₹22.3 cr, ₹116.2 cr, ₹168.0 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh6.finding: Operating cash flow was ₹15.4 cr in FY26, about 30% of the ₹51.8 cr profit, after negative flows in FY24 and FY25.

pr1.finding: Profit after tax grew about 123% in FY26, to ₹51.8 cr from ₹23.3 cr.

pr2.finding: Net margin improved from 3.76% (FY24) to 6.62% (FY25) and 9.61% (FY26).

pr3.finding: Return on net worth was 30.83% in FY26.

pr5.finding: Peer margins were not found in public sources.

va1.finding: Post-issue P/E of about 17.6x (₹912 cr market cap on FY26 profit) vs a peer median of 21.9x (Senco 9.6x, TBZ 19.6x, PNGS Reva 24.2x, Motisons 27.8x).

va2.finding: Post-issue price to book of about 2.26x (₹912 cr market cap vs about ₹403 cr post-issue net worth) vs a peer median of 3.9x.

va3.finding: Peer market cap to sales figures were not found in public sources.

va4.finding: Only bonus issues (May and December 2025) were found; no priced share issues or transfers in the 12 months before the IPO were found in public sources.

pg1.finding: Promoters hold about 69.8% after the issue, down from 100%.

pg2.finding: No information on pledged promoter shares was found.

pg3.finding: Related-party transaction figures were not found in public sources.

pg4.finding: No information on regulatory action against promoters was found.

is1.finding: The offer for sale is ₹55.08 cr, or 20% of the ₹275.4 cr issue.

is2.finding: The issue is about 30.2% of the ₹912 cr post-issue market cap.

is3.finding: The promoter selling shareholder's average cost is ₹18.31 a share, so the upper band is about 8.8x cost.

up1.finding: ₹152.84 cr, or 69.4% of the fresh issue, funds inventory for a new Maharashtra showroom and an expanded Gujarat showroom.

up2.finding: ₹30 cr, or 13.6% of the fresh issue, goes to repaying borrowings.

up3.finding: General corporate purposes take ₹37.48 cr, or 17.0% of the fresh issue.

up4.finding: Public sources don't say whose loans are being repaid.

lg1.finding: Litigation amounts were not found in public sources.

lg2.finding: No information on criminal or regulatory cases was found.

lg3.finding: Contingent liabilities were ₹5.0 cr at June 2026, about 2.7% of the ₹183 cr net worth.

rk1.finding: All revenue comes from walk-in sales at its own showrooms; the concentration called out is geographic (Ahmedabad showrooms 67.97% of FY26 revenue), not by customer.

rk2.finding: It relies entirely on third-party manufacturers and karigars with no long-term contracts, which is called out as a risk; supplier shares are not published.

rk3.finding: Operating since 2012 (about 14 years), and the promoter has run the jewellery business since 1999.

rk4.finding: Auditor remarks were not found in public sources.
